Get a composed map of Portugal

Source: R/get_map.R
get_map.Rd

Returns an sf object with mainland Portugal and the islands moved next to it as insets, ready for plotting. Uses the pre-simplified bundled datasets.

Usage

get_map(
  level = "municipio",
  islands = "compact",
  data = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  fuzzy = FALSE,
  aliases = NULL,
  admin_vintage = NULL,
  nuts_vintage = NULL,
  client = NULL
)

Arguments

level

Administrative level: "freguesia", "municipio", "distrito", "nuts1", "nuts2", "nuts3" — or one of the health geographies dissolved from freguesias via pt_health_codes: "uls", "reg_saude" (regiões de saúde) for the 2024 reform, or "aces". If you have data by municipality, you might need "uls_municipio" and "aces_municipio": the units that share a municipality are merged into one (see vignette("health-geographies")). Health levels are defined on the 2025 map only.

islands

How to show the Açores and Madeira: "compact" (the default), "groups", "box", "in_place" or "none" (mainland only), or a layout made with island_layout() for anything else, such as a different setting per archipelago or no frames.

data

Optional data.frame to join onto the boundaries, producing a map ready for a choropleth. Requires by.

by

How to join data: which column identifies the unit and what it contains. Same forms as pt_join(). The unit keyword must correspond to level. Rows of data for an archipelago left out with "none" are dropped without a warning.

fuzzy

Logical. Enable fuzzy name matching for the join (see pt_match()). Default FALSE.

aliases

Optional named character vector of extra name aliases for the join (see pt_match()).

admin_vintage

Which freguesia map to draw. Available values are "2025" (the default, the bundled data) or "2013", the map in force from the 2013 reform until freguesias were restored in 2025. The 2013 map is downloaded from DGT (CAOP 2024, the last release that used the 2013 freguesias division), simplified and cached the first time, which needs the rmapshaper package and an internet connection. For "2011" and "2001" maps, use INE's BGRI by merging census areas of that year instead (see get_censos()), or convert the data with pt_recode(). Names in data are matched against this vintage. See vignette("vintages").

nuts_vintage

Which NUTS revision to use: "2024" (the default), "2013" or "2002". Independent of admin_vintage, because every revision groups whole municipalities.

client

Optional GeoClient to download and cache with (for a custom cache directory).

Value

An sf object in WGS84 (EPSG:4326).

Details

Every result has the same columns, in the same order, whatever the options: the level's own columns (and any joined data), then geopt_type, geopt_label and geopt_frame_level, then the geometry. geopt_type is "boundary" for the regions and "frame" for the frames drawn around the insets (see island_layout()). geopt_label holds a frame's name, or the label of an archipelago drawn as a rectangle (islands = "box").

For a map of one region, filter the result: rows keep their codes and names. For an archipelago, use islands = "in_place" first, so it is in its true position rather than moved and enlarged.

See also

island_layout(), plot_pt()

Examples

library(ggplot2)

m <- get_map("municipio")
ggplot(m) + geom_sf()
#> Warning: 'x' is NULL so the result will be NULL


# Mainland only
m <- get_map("municipio", islands = "none")

# Regions and frames drawn separately
m <- get_map("nuts2")
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = m[m$geopt_type == "boundary", ], aes(fill = nuts2)) +
  geom_sf(data = m[m$geopt_type == "frame", ], fill = NA, linewidth = 0.5)


# The archipelagos as labelled rectangles
get_map("nuts3", islands = "box")

# Join your own data by municipality name
df <- data.frame(concelho = c("Porto", "Lisboa"), value = c(10, 20))
m <- get_map("municipio", data = df, by = c(municipio = "concelho"))
#> get_map: 306 boundaries have no data row (NA fill).
ggplot(m) + geom_sf(aes(fill = value))
#> Warning: 'x' is NULL so the result will be NULL


# The NUTS 3 regions of the 2013 revision (25, against 26 today)
get_map("nuts3", nuts_vintage = "2013")
